around.headline: Thief breaks into Bengaluru PG, escapes with 12 phones and 7 laptops
around.summary: A thief sneaked into a paying guest accommodation in Bengaluru and got away with 12 phones and 7 laptops, per The Times of India. If you live in a PG or shared flat, don't rely on the building's common-door lock alone — add your own lock on your room door and never leave laptops or phones out when you step away, even briefly.

around.headline: Wipro Bengaluru Marathon runs today — expect road closures
around.summary: The city's 13th edition Wipro Bengaluru Marathon takes place this morning, per The Hindu. Even if you're not running, plan for diversions and heavier traffic along the route through the morning.

around.headline: Varthur Road to be asphalted before flyover work; task force for ORR bottlenecks
around.summary: Authorities have been told to asphalt Varthur Road before starting flyover construction amid civic backlash, and a separate task force is being formed to tackle chronic Varthur-Gunjur bottlenecks, per The Hindu and The Times of India. Commuters on this stretch should expect continued disruption in the near term even as fixes are planned.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Bank strike Sept 28–30: PSU banks waive ATM charges above free limit
around.summary: Public sector banks will waive charges on ATM withdrawals beyond the free monthly limit for three days from September 28, coinciding with a bank strike, per Moneycontrol. Worth withdrawing any cash you'll need over the next few days beforehand, since branch services may be affected.

around.headline: Electoral roll row escalates: Congress, NDA allies press EC for clarity
around.summary: Congress protested in Bengaluru demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation, while NDA allies including HD Kumaraswamy pushed the Election Commission for clarity on the ongoing voter-list revision (SIR), per NDTV and Telegraph India. If you haven't already, check the draft electoral roll for your address to confirm your name hasn't been dropped, and file a correction before the window closes.

around.headline: China, US agree to AI dialogue and tariff cuts on $30 billion in goods
around.summary: During Xi Jinping's visit, China and the US agreed to start an AI dialogue and cut tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods, per Reuters. A thaw in US-China trade tension can eventually feed through to prices of imported electronics and components here, though any effect will take time to show up.

street_smart.title: You live in a shared PG (paying guest) accommodation in Bengaluru. The main gate is often propped open during the day for deliveries and visitors, and your room only has the flimsy stock latch it came with. You're stepping out for a quick errand, leaving your phone charger, laptop and a spare phone in the room.
street_smart.based_on: Thief sneaks into paying guest accommodation in Bengaluru, escapes with 12 phones & 7 laptops — The Times of India, September 26, 2026.
street_smart.situation: There's no dedicated security guard at the gate during the day, and several other tenants' rooms on your floor also use only the original latch that came fitted with the room.

choices.text: Leave as is — the gate is usually watched informally, and it's just a quick errand.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. PG thefts like the one that hit 12 phones and 7 laptops happen precisely because common doors are left open for convenience and individual rooms rely on a stock latch that takes seconds to force — 'just a quick errand' is exactly the window thieves use, and by the time anyone notices the door was propped open, they're gone with everything of value from multiple rooms.

choices.text: Fit your own additional keyed padlock on your room door, keep valuables you're not carrying in a small lockbox, and flag the propped-open gate to the PG manager.
choices.feedback: Correct. A second, independent lock defeats the 'force the flimsy stock latch' method that makes single-room security so easy to beat, a lockbox protects what's inside even if the door does give way, and reporting the open gate addresses the root cause for the whole floor, not just your room.

choices.text: Take your laptop and both phones with you rather than leaving them, but don't say anything about the open gate.
choices.feedback: Risky. Carrying your own valuables helps you personally, but it does nothing for your roommates or the next theft — and an unaddressed propped-open gate means the same opportunity stays open for whoever the thief targets next.

choices.text: Ask a neighbouring tenant to keep an eye on the floor while you're out.
choices.feedback: Risky. A neighbour has their own day to get on with and won't be watching continuously — it's a marginal help at best, not a real deterrent, and it doesn't fix the weak lock or the open gate that made the theft possible in the first place.

takeaways: Add your own keyed padlock or a secondary lock on top of whatever latch the PG provides — stock room locks are built for privacy, not security, and are routinely forced in seconds.
Report a propped-open or unmanned main gate to the PG owner/manager immediately; it's a risk to every tenant, not just you, and owners are often unaware how long it's been left that way.
If something is stolen, file a police FIR right away — it's required for any insurance claim and for blocking a stolen phone's IMEI via the CEIR portal (ceir.gov.in) so it can't be reused.

quiz.question: A thief who broke into a Bengaluru PG accommodation this week got away with 12 phones and how many laptops?
quiz.why: PG and shared-accommodation thefts often net multiple tenants' devices in one break-in, which is why filing an FIR fast matters — it's usually the only way to get a stolen phone's IMEI blacklisted before it's resold.

quiz.question: Starting September 28, PSU banks will waive charges on ATM withdrawals above the free limit for how many days, coinciding with a bank strike?
quiz.why: The free-limit waiver is meant to cushion customers during the strike window, when branch counters may be short-staffed or shut.

quiz.question: Which Bengaluru road has been ordered to be asphalted before flyover construction begins, after civic backlash?
quiz.why: Varthur Road is also part of the wider Varthur-Gunjur stretch getting a dedicated task force to tackle its chronic traffic bottlenecks.

quiz.question: Which constitutional body is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India?
quiz.why: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body set up under Article 324, currently headed by the Chief Election Commissioner alongside two Election Commissioners.

quiz.question: Which river is Bengaluru's main source of piped drinking water, pumped over 100 km and lifted nearly 500 metres in elevation to reach the city?
quiz.why: Because the water has to be lifted so high before it reaches Bengaluru, pumping it from the Cauvery is extremely energy-intensive — a major recurring cost for BWSSB.
